layout_note: A SHORT, SELF-CONTAINED proemial section titled (italic) 'Concerning interpretation of holie Scriptures .', printed on the LOWER HALF of page 14 (printed folio '14') of the 1610 OT2 (Second Tome) front matter. It is bounded ABOVE and BELOW by a horizontal rule: above the top rule is the TAIL of the preceding 'PROEMIAL ANNOTATIONS vpon the Booke of Pſalmes' (whose first page = matter-ot2-preface-psalms, page_index 3), ending '...render al praiſe to God.'; below the bottom rule the volume proceeds to 'THE BOOKE OF PSALMES / PSALME I.' on page_index 15. Thus this is the LAST front-matter item before the Psalter text proper, and it is DISTINCT from the Psalms Proemial Annotations. Because the page's running header ('PROEMIAL ANNOTATIONS', folio '14' top-left) belongs to the section ENDING above the rule, this section has no running header of its own. LAYOUT: one wide column of roman prose, opening with a large ~3-line drop-cap 'A' (AS Prophecie…), followed by four further short paragraphs, EACH closing with an italic patristic source-citation and EACH keyed to a small ROMAN summary note in the LEFT margin (five notes; the page's TWO OTHER left-margin notes — 'Other inſtrumentes make conſorte with the Pſalter.' and 'Al vertues are referred to Gods honour.' — sit ABOVE the top rule and belong to the Psalms annotations, so they are EXCLUDED here). TWO GLYPH REGIMES: (a) roman body sets a REAL connected 'w' (verified per-instance: was, wil, wherwith, written, which, wordes, knowlege); (b) italic apparatus — the parenthetical glosses ('or other holie Scripture', 'Prophetes', 'nor explication'), the leading word 'Neither', and every source-citation — contains no 'w', so no vv/w call arises in the italic. Punctuation is TIGHT (no French spacing) at the section's colons/semicolons/commas (verified: 'Ghoſt:', 'truth;', 'Scripture,is'); the ONLY spaced high-mark is the heading terminal ('Scriptures .'). ct is always a ligature (Sainctes, expect, Doct., Ezech.). The modern scanner watermark 'www.fatimamovement.com' and a small red heraldic shield overlaid at the lower-left corner are digitisation marks, NOT part of the original page; excluded.

uncertain.note: The heading's terminal mark, preceded by a clear space, is read as a PERIOD — consistent with every other section heading in this corpus ending in a point (APPROBATIO. / '…vpon the Booke of Pſalmes.' / 'THE ARGVMENT OF GENESIS.'), and the highest-zoom (4.5x) view shows a compact baseline dot. A COMMA cannot be fully excluded: a lower/medium zoom (3x) suggested a slight tail. Medium-high confidence on period; the preceding space is real (this edition's occasional space-before-punctuation habit).

The Augustine citation opens with a LOWERCASE italic 's.' (verified against the capital 'S.' of the Ierom, Amb. and Greg. citations on the same page — a genuine compositor inconsistency, preserved). NO period is visible after 'Aug' (transcribed 'Aug ſer.'); a very faint dropped/lost point at this raster cannot be 100% excluded. The abbreviation intends 'S. Aug. ser. 18. de verb. Domini' (Augustine, Sermo 18 de verbis Domini). Medium-high confidence on the lowercase s; medium on the absent Aug-period.
Italic '(nor explication)' — read letter-by-letter e-x-p-l-i-c-a-t-i-o-n at 3x; the small italic fount makes the '-ation' tail lightly inked but the reading is secure. High confidence.

method: Four validations. (1) LOCALIZATION: paged the OT2 front matter via ocr-spike/jp2_page.py archive-ot2-1610 (pages 3-16). The Psalms 'PROEMIAL ANNOTATIONS' run pages 3-14a; on page_index 14, after they close ('…render al praiſe to God.'), a horizontal rule introduces a NEW italic-headed section 'Concerning interpretation of holie Scriptures .' with its own drop-cap and patristic paragraphs, closed by a second rule — confirmed by heading + content to be a SEPARATE proemial section on Scripture interpretation, NOT the Psalms annotations (which are the matter-ot2-preface-psalms locus, page 3) and NOT duplicated. (2) IDENTITY: archive-ot2-1610 S1 maps (jp2_page.py) to 'S01_1582-first-edition-3vol/…2 of 3 1610 Old Testament_jp2' = the 1610 Second Tome; the surrounding pages (Approbatio p.2, Psalms Proemial Annotations pp.3-14, THE BOOKE OF PSALMES p.15) confirm the 1610 OT2 front matter. Read from the native jp2 raster (3334×4684, ~400-DPI class). (3) PLACEMENT: printed folio '14' (verso; page running-header 'PROEMIAL ANNOTATIONS' belongs to the section ending above the top rule, so this section carries no header of its own); it is the LAST front-matter item before 'THE BOOKE OF PSALMES / PSALME I.' which begins on page_index 15. (4) COMPLETENESS: the ENTIRE section is on page 14, fully enclosed between the two horizontal rules — heading + drop-cap paragraph (2 Pet 1 / Ioan 14.16 / 1 Cor 12) + four short cited paragraphs (Jerome, Augustine, Ambrose, Gregory), each with a left-margin gloss; nothing continues onto page 15 (which starts the Psalter text). Diplomatic per GUIDELINES.md: long-ſ glyph-driven; w/vv per-instance (all body w real, verified by stroke-connectivity at 2.5-3x); ct→component letters; u/v period-swap and i/j kept as printed; French spacing checked at every colon/semicolon/comma (all tight except the spaced heading terminal); Latin/italic citations transcribed exactly; printer's variant (lowercase 's.' citation) preserved. Region crops zoomed 1.8-4.5x with autocontrast on faint marks. No content-anchor reference (janvier/Madueke) applies to this non-scriptural matter section.
confidence: high on the heading text, the five paragraphs, and the section boundaries — localization / identity / placement / completeness all PASS. High on long-ſ placement (hand-verified, glyph-driven) and on the real-w regime (per-instance stroke-connectivity). Medium-high on the small-fount italic citations (verified at 2.8-3x). Two flagged items: the heading terminal mark (period vs comma; period committed on corpus consistency) and the lowercase 's.'/absent Aug-period in the line-12 citation (preserved as printed).
